sections: Global authority lock order and retained observations

repo_truth: Fresh isolated contract review 4 returned CLEAN for the exact identity, operation allocation, two-branch preflight, and distinct unsafe-recovery refusal contracts. Engine already depends on getrandom and SHA-256. Compiler setup creates or preserves `.handbook` and optionally resets only planned runtime-state paths; no repository identity service or file exists. A separate retained-authority promotion lane is adding reusable crate-private ordered-lock/recovery observation APIs and may still be active.
allowed_scope: Add `crates/engine/src/repository_invocation_identity.rs`, export its reviewed public types/service from engine lib, and add focused engine tests.
Edit compiler setup/lib and focused compiler setup tests to initialize or preserve the identity only on mutation-admitted setup outcomes.
Edit CLI setup rendering or add focused CLI setup tests only if an existing typed setup error projection must be extended after GitNexus impact.
Consume the retained-authority lane's crate-private lock/recovery/complete-registry observation APIs; coordinate missing interfaces with the parent instead of editing authority modules.
non_goals: Do not edit registry/approval/promotion/lifecycle authority modules, compiler charter product, approver CLI, Flow, definitions, docs, proof/control/handoff/ledger files, or HCM-2.3.
Do not accept caller repository identity, raw allocator token, operation ID, entropy, path-derived identity, environment identity, or fixture identity in production.
Do not change frozen Admin/approval/public promotion request schemas, add a dependency, or commit.
tasks: Run GitNexus upstream impact before every existing-symbol edit and report any HIGH/CRITICAL boundary before proceeding.

Write RED tests that independently reproduce the exact repository identity and five operation-ID vectors, all five typed operation mappings, byte lengths, entropy failure, closed preflight and recovery-refusal serialization/nullability/substitution negatives, and direct-engine opaque-ID compatibility boundary.

Implement `RepositoryInvocationOperationV1`, exact engine-owned identity/operation allocation outputs, `RepositoryInvocationPreflightResultV1`, and distinct `RepositoryInvocationRecoveryRefusalV1`; use fresh OS entropy in production and deterministic injected entropy only in tests.

Implement strict bounded no-follow identity observation and setup-only create-new initialization at `.handbook/repository-identity.v1` with same-parent temporary file, file fsync, atomic rename, parent fsync, exact 71 bytes, concurrency convergence, byte preservation, and unsafe-evidence refusal.

Under retained promotion+registry locks, run the one shared predecessor-ordered registry/approval recovery path before every identity read; before bootstrap admit valid file identity, after bootstrap require exact equality to the complete committed registry-chain state. Project unsafe recovery into the exact recovery-refusal envelope and identity/entropy failures into the exact preflight branches.

Integrate setup so create/refresh initializes or preserves identity only when setup may mutate, `--reset-state` never selects it, existing SetupOutcome semantics remain compatible, and focused compiler/CLI setup tests prove creation, preservation, tamper/unsafe/entropy/concurrency failure, and reset exclusion.
Run focused engine identity tests, compiler setup tests, CLI setup tests if changed, cargo check for engine/compiler/CLI, rustfmt check, and clippy for changed targets.
contracts_and_gates: Only setup initializes identity; every product operation only reads it and allocates one fresh ID.
Mandatory recovery precedes identity resolution and can emit only the distinct exact recovery refusal; it never fabricates preflight or normal results.
Preflight/recovery refusal paths perform zero native calls and create no new current-operation-owned delta.
Compiler/CLI pass only the typed engine operation and never implement derivation or authority.
stop_conditions: Stop and report before any HIGH/CRITICAL existing-symbol edit, public contract widening, or duplicate authority/recovery implementation.

If the retained-authority lane has not yet exposed a safe reusable crate-private API, complete only disjoint pure identity/DTO tests and implementation, then report the exact missing interface to the parent rather than editing its files.
